name: Metalinguistic more … than
pattern: more XP than YP with competing descriptions of one item

entry.name: Metalinguistic more … than
entry.pattern: more XP than YP with competing descriptions of one item

1.definition: Ranks alternative descriptions by their appropriateness.

examples.form: The proposal was [more optimistic than realistic].

projection.target: The same referent is evaluated under alternative labels. Even expressions lacking a common numerical scale can be compared for adequacy of description.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Choosing the better description with more than
curious.summary: More ... than can compare two descriptions of the same thing and say which one fits better.
curious.body: In The proposal was more optimistic than realistic, the speaker is weighing two labels for the same proposal and saying that optimistic fits better than realistic. Here there is one thing, the proposal, and two competing descriptions of it. The descriptions don't have to share a numerical scale, yet they can still be compared for how well each one describes the thing.

examples.text: The proposal was [more optimistic than realistic].
The meal was [more filling than tasty].

curious.try: Think of something you've seen or eaten. Can you say which of two descriptions fits it better, using more ... than?

teacher.summary: Helps explain more ... than used to rank two descriptions of one item.
teacher.explain: In this metalinguistic use, more XP than YP ranks alternative descriptions by their appropriateness: The proposal was more optimistic than realistic. The same referent is evaluated under two labels, and expressions lacking a common numerical scale can still be compared for adequacy of description. This dictionary relates the pattern to than-reduced clauses and to gradation.
teacher.terms: Sometimes called a metalinguistic comparative. In this dictionary: metalinguistic more ... than.

examples.text: The proposal was [more optimistic than realistic].
The meal was [more filling than tasty].

contrasts.text: The proposal was more optimistic than realistic.
The new proposal was more optimistic than the old one.

watch_for: A learner might read more optimistic than realistic as comparing two different things, when it weighs two descriptions of the same thing.
A learner might try to find a second item to compare, when the comparison is between two labels for one referent.
teacher.activity: Students write sentences with more X than Y about a film, a meal or a plan, choosing two adjectives that could both describe it. They explain why one fits better.

checked.note: Fixed: removed the claim that an ordinary comparison sets two things side by side or compares on one scale, which the entry does not state; the texts now say only that the pattern weighs two descriptions of one item.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Metalinguistic more … than." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/metalinguistic-more-than-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
